subject.title: Gmail hook sessions / Signal inbox notifications stop working after update to 2026.3.31

question: Should this Gmail-to-Signal regression be resolved by accepting the opt-in Gmail Pub/Sub pull-delivery direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90723, or by repairing the existing push/session-key path instead?
rationale: Both paths touch public hook ingress, session routing, secrets, and operator setup behavior; the code evidence shows the current behavior is not fixed, but automation should not choose the permanent Gmail delivery contract alone.

options.title: Land Opt-In Pull Delivery
options.body: Accept the proof-positive pull-mode PR after RFC and gog runtime availability are confirmed, while leaving push as the default until later soak.

options.title: Repair Push Path First
options.body: Keep the current push watcher contract and require a focused live repro/root-cause fix for the Pub/Sub push to Signal failure before adding a new delivery mode.

options.title: Pause For More Live Diagnostics
options.body: Ask reporters to capture the exact gog watcher-side failure logs before choosing between push repair and pull delivery.

recommendation.title: Land Opt-In Pull Delivery
recommendation.body: Accept the proof-positive pull-mode PR after RFC and gog runtime availability are confirmed, while leaving push as the default until later soak.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history across Gmail setup, watcher lifecycle, and the security-sensitive delivery decision surface.
